question: Should Crabbox ship a direct GitHub Codespaces provider that requires a `codespace`-scoped GitHub credential and makes the local operator responsible for Codespaces billing, retention, and claim-owned deletion?
rationale: The implementation can be technically reviewed, but accepting a new paid direct-provider surface and its destructive cleanup policy is a product and operational boundary that source inspection cannot decide.

options.title: Authorize live validation and decide after proof
options.body: Grant the scoped validation credential, inspect redacted exact-head lifecycle evidence, and decide whether to ship the documented direct-provider boundary.

options.title: Keep the provider out of core for now
options.body: Leave this PR open or close it only after a maintainer decides that a Codespaces integration should remain external rather than built in.

recommendation.title: Authorize live validation and decide after proof
recommendation.body: Grant the scoped validation credential, inspect redacted exact-head lifecycle evidence, and decide whether to ship the documented direct-provider boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows steipete carried the provider’s safety and integration repairs and is best positioned to route the product-boundary decision.
